sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The target student population was Grade 8 students (approximately age 14) where the average age in Grade 8 was at least 13.5; otherwise Grade 9 became the target population. Sampling followed a two-stage cluster design: PPS sampling of schools within each country, then random selection of an intact class from the target grade within each sampled school with all students in that class surveyed. The report also applies participation-rate criteria (85% selected schools and 85% selected students within participating schools, with a weighted overall participation rate of 75%) and uses replacement schools when needed to meet response-rate requirements. The excerpt does not specify additional analytic exclusions (e.g., missing item rules) beyond these design and participation criteria.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 International Report documents the ICCS study design and the measurement framework for civic and citizenship education. The student cognitive test comprised 80 items (79 used in analysis) covering four content domains (civic society and systems, civic principles, civic participation, civic identities) and two cognitive processes (knowing; reasoning and analyzing), with items administered via a balanced rotated booklet design (45 minutes per student). The report also describes affective-behavioral outcomes measured through a 40-minute student questionnaire using Likert-type items, with questionnaire scales set to an international metric (mean 50, SD 10 for equally weighted national samples). Sampling was two-stage cluster sampling with PPS school selection and intact-class selection within schools, targeting Grade 8 (or Grade 9 when average Grade 8 age was below 13.5). Results presented include country comparisons of civic knowledge scale scores (mean 500, SD 100 for equally weighted national samples) and proficiency-level distributions, plus descriptive cross-country patterns for democratic values, trust, civic engagement, and related attitudes.
